1. Heading and placement: Using an unnumbered `## Glossary` heading (parallel to the unnumbered `## Changelog` heading at line 729) leaves sections `## 1.` through `## 12.` intact and keeps lines 1-727 unchanged.

Non-normative authority framing: Open `## Glossary` with an explicit statement that the glossary is a reader aid summarizing terms defined in `§§1-12` and the serialization specifications referenced in `§6.2`; it creates no independent obligation, and if any summary disagrees with `§§1-12` or a controlling FounderOS decision named in `§11`, the operative section and controlling decision govern.

interfaces_and_contracts:
No TypeScript interfaces, wire protocols, database schemas, or binary serialization formats (`BRJ:a:1`, `BRJ:b:1`, `BRJ:c:1`, `BRJ:c:2`, `BRJ:d:1`) are modified.

Within `docs/command-journal-contract.md`, the new `## Glossary` section must define each term strictly in accordance with the existing contract text:
- `ambiguous` / `mismatch` / `reconciled`: The consumed 3.5 reconciliation semantics carried on a `resolved` command event (`§5.2`, lines 374-377) and at the `build_room_events` cross-store boundary (`§1.4`, lines 100-106), where `ambiguous` never resolves silently and `mismatch` is surfaced without auto-resolution.
- `authorization_ref`: Governing authorization reference on `journaled` and `decision` rows (`§2` element 7, line 144; `§2`, line 162); for `completed` (directly or via `resolved`), must resolve to a valid, applicable authorization whose granted scope covers the observed `(provider, model, execution_surface)` (`§5.3`, lines 387-413).
- `BRJ:c:1` and `BRJ:c:2`: Version identifiers of serialization specification (c) for command-class event rows (`packages/journal/specs/serialization-c-command-row.md` and `packages/journal/specs/serialization-c-command-row-v2.md`), prefixing each command row's canonical bytes; `BRJ:c:2` adds `init_model` and `provider_conversation_id` on `dispatched`, and a chain's command rows move from `BRJ:c:1` to `BRJ:c:2` at most once and never back (`§6.2`, lines 510-517).
- `build_room_events`: The ratified `DEC-20260815-11` lifecycle event log table, authoritative for room lifecycle transitions, guards, and resulting states, distinct from the command journal (`§1.4`, lines 64-110).
- `chain_hash`: 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 digest over the prior row's 64-byte lowercase-hex ASCII `chain_hash` (or the 64-ASCII-`0` genesis constant on the first row) concatenated with the row's canonical byte sequence under spec (c) or spec (d) (`§4.1`, lines 273-290; `§6.2`, lines 495-507).
- `command` (record class): The record class for governed commands on the canonical journal chain, represented as an event-sourced sequence of command events sharing a `command_id` (`§1.2`, lines 50-58; `§2`, lines 114-148; `§5.2`, lines 359-377).
- `command_envelope`: The post-redaction normalized command representation carried as canonical bytes per specification (a) on `journaled` rows, never containing raw secrets (`§2` element 6, line 143; `§6.1`, lines 463-467; `§6.2`, lines 472, 499-500).
- `command_id`: Dedicated `cmd_`-prefixed command identifier (`§2` element 1, line 138) and end-to-end dispatch idempotency key enforcing at-most-once execution across gateway and adapter boundaries (`§5.3`, lines 428-432); not applicable to `decision` records (`§2`, lines 211-215).
- `command_journal_chain_head`: Singleton Postgres table (`head_id` primary key with `CHECK (head_id = 1)`) storing the mutable append serialization latch (`seq` and `chain_hash`), initialized to `seq = 0` and 64 ASCII `0`s by migration, holding no journal authority (`§3`, lines 228-231; `§4.1`, lines 304-328).
- `command_journal_events`: Dedicated append-only Postgres table storing one row per journal event in global `seq` order, with `UPDATE` and `DELETE` denied to all application roles and trigger-enforced (`§3`, lines 227-235; `§4.1`, lines 277-287, 329-332).
- `command_journal_writer`: Dedicated database role that is the sole role granted `INSERT` on `command_journal_events` and `UPDATE` on `command_journal_chain_head`, with all other application roles explicitly revoked (`§3`, lines 236-247; `§4.1`, lines 322-325).
- `completed`: Terminal command-class event requiring a prior `dispatched` row, an observed routing identity matching the journaled intended routing identity, and a resolved `authorization_ref` covering the observed `(provider, model, execution_surface)` (`§2`, lines 130-134; `§5.2`, lines 373-374; `§5.3`, lines 387-413).
- `decision` (record class): Single-event, terminal-by-construction record class on the canonical journal chain for Founder decision acts (`T4` `plan.revision_requested`, `T5` `plan.approved`, `T22` `founder.cancel`), carrying actor `founder`, the decision, recorded lifecycle state (and `prior_state` when `RECONCILING`), conditional `plan_hash`, `authorization_ref`, `lifecycle_event_ref`, and timestamps, with elements 1, 4, 8, and 9 not applicable (`§1.2`, lines 50-54; `§2`, lines 153-218; `§6.2(d)`, lines 477-489; `§12`, lines 691-727).
- `dispatch_state`: Derived view equal to the latest event's type for a command, never stored as a mutable column (`§2` element 8, line 145; `§5.4`, lines 444-450).
- `dispatched`: Command-class event (at most once, after `journaled` and any `identity_bound`) recording the observed actual `provider`, `model`, and `execution_surface`, plus `init_model` and `provider_conversation_id` under `BRJ:c:2` where reported (`§2` element 4, lines 126-130, 141; `§5.2`, lines 371-372; `§5.3`, lines 380-381).
- `Effective plan-bearing state`: The recorded lifecycle state at a `decision` act, with `RECONCILING` resolved single-step to its stored `prior_state`; governs `plan_hash` presence on `decision` records (absent in the derived no-PlanDoc states `ROOM_CREATED`, `SCOPED`, `PLANNING`; required otherwise; fail-closed if `RECONCILING` has no available `prior_state`) (`§2`, lines 165-206).
- `envelope_digest`: 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 digest over the canonical bytes of `command_envelope` per specification (a) (`§2` element 6, line 143; `§6.2`, lines 495-500).
- `failed`: Terminal command-class event carrying a failure classification after `dispatched`, or directly after `journaled` / `identity_bound` only when the attempt provably never left the gateway boundary (`§5.2`, lines 373-374; `§5.3`, lines 414-418).
- `Genesis chain hash`: The constant of 64 ASCII `0` characters used as the prior-hash input for the first row (`seq = 1`) and as the migration-initialized hash in `command_journal_chain_head` (`§4.1`, lines 288-290, 306-309; `§6.2`, lines 504-506).
- `identity_bound`: Optional one-time command-class event between `journaled` and `dispatched` that binds element-2 identities (`room_id`, `run_id`, `execution_id`) not yet existing at `journaled` (`§2`, lines 121-126; `§5.2`, lines 367-371; `§5.3`, lines 379-380).
- `init_model`: The model named by the executor's init event before work is sent, recorded on `dispatched` under `BRJ:c:2` alongside `provider_conversation_id` (`§2` element 4, line 141; `§6.2`, lines 510-514; Changelog `v0.18`, lines 731-739).
- `journaled`: Mandatory first command-class event for a `command_id`, durably committed before dispatch (`§5.1`, lines 352-354) and carrying immutable elements 1, 3, 5-7, any existing element-2 identities, and intended routing identity (`§2`, lines 117-128; `§5.2`, lines 364-366).
- `lifecycle_event_ref`: Normative pair `(`room_id`, `event_id`)` referencing the corresponding `build_room_events` row (`build_room_events_event_id_unique UNIQUE (room_id, event_id)`), committed in the same Neon transaction when created by the same control-plane act (`§1.4`, lines 81-99).
- `outcome`: Derived terminal determination for a command (`completed` or `failed` directly or via `resolved`, `unresolved` while unreconciled, and pending otherwise), computed from the command's event sequence (`§2` element 9, line 146; `§5.4`, lines 444-450).
- `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN`: Existing Founder-held control-plane credential (at least 32 characters, distinct from `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN`, enforced in `packages/control-plane/src/config.ts`) required by `§8.2` to authenticate Founder plan decisions in Phase 4 (`§8.2`, lines 562-575).
- `plan_hash`: 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 digest over the canonical PlanDoc byte sequence per specification (b) (`§6.2`, lines 472, 501-502), computed at `T3`, matched at `T5`, and conditionally carried on `decision` records (`§2`, lines 165-206; `§7.1`, lines 527-530; `§8.2`, lines 555-562).
- `prior_state`: The pre-`RECONCILING` lifecycle state resolved when a `decision` record is written from `RECONCILING` and recorded positively on the row alongside the recorded state (`§2`, lines 169-183, 199-203).
- `provider_conversation_id`: The provider's conversation identifier from the executor's init event, recorded on `dispatched` under `BRJ:c:2` alongside `init_model` (`§2` element 4, line 141; `§6.2`, lines 510-514).
- `record_class`: Explicit discriminator field (`command` or `decision`) carried on every journal row and encoded inside the canonical byte input to `chain_hash` (`§2`, lines 215-218; `§6.2`, lines 487-489).
- `recorded_at`: Server-generated timestamp on every journal row (`§2` element 11, line 148).
- `resolved`: Terminal command-class event permitted at most once and only after `unresolved`, carrying the reconciled determination (`completed` or `failed`) and reconciliation semantics (`reconciled`, `ambiguous`, or `mismatch`) (`§5.2`, lines 374-377; `§5.3`, lines 382-383, 407-413).
- `seq`: Server-generated global sequence number ordering all `command` and `decision` rows on the single canonical journal chain (`§1.2`, lines 50-53; `§2` element 11, line 148; `§4.1`, lines 284-300, 329).
- `unresolved`: Command-class event appended after `journaled`, `identity_bound`, or `dispatched` when provider contact cannot be ruled out or authorization coverage is indeterminate; blocks any success claim, retry, or completion representation until `resolved` (`§5.2`, lines 373-377; `§5.3`, lines 400-402, 419-425; `§5.5`, lines 451-455).
